budget.rule: the replay bounds actually in force (max_commands, max_input_bytes, max_output_bytes, max_wall_seconds) plus the executed command count; a search budget is never inferred

denominator.rule: sha256(json.dumps(sorted(point identities), separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=True)) over the DUT points only

point_identity.rule: one identity per Verilator point: the saved field map with the source path made relative to the build inputs/ root, serialised as json.dumps(fields, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))

source_set.rule: rows of {"path", "sha256"} for the declared structural-build DUT source files in declared order, path relative to the build inputs/ root; digest = sha256(json.dumps(rows, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")))

workload.rule: recorded command lines with the 32-hex execution nonce replaced by {NONCE}; digest = sha256("\n".join(lines) + "\n") over ASCII

external_contract.claim: No second tool produced a measurement under this contract; the synthetic documents below are validator self-tests, not measurements, and no external covered/total is published.
requirements: the other tool's offline line/block measurement of the same DUT source files (dut.source_files_sha256), same normalised point set (dut.point_set_sha256) and same canonical denominator (dut.denominator_sha256)
that tool's replay of the identical recorded command sequence (workload.commands_sha256) with its command count and local ticks
the identical replay budget in force and the executed command count
an explicit mode declaration (only offline recorded-prefix replay is comparable here; online and fixed_time are rejected)
raw artifact SHA256s and the exact reproduction command

schema.description: A second tool's offline line/block measurement of one of our measured DUT scopes, for comparison under dut-line-block/offline-recorded-prefix.v1.
schema.title: external_coverage_measurement.v1

self_tests.note: Each scope runs the same synthetic case set: one document that reproduces the measured identity exactly (must be comparable) and mismatching ones that must be rejected for the named reason.

steps_for_third_party: read one scope record from this package and from docs/reports/coverage-comparison-contract-20261030.json: it names the component, the declared DUT source files (dut.source_files_sha256) and the canonical denominator (dut.denominator_sha256)

build the same DUT from the same pinned cache inputs and instrument line/block points with Verilator --coverage-line exactly as described by the scope measurement's coverage.json (build_argv carries --coverage-line; point kinds line/branch, all hierarchy instances retained)
replay the identical recorded command sequence, normalise the 32-hex execution nonce and publish workload.commands_sha256, workload.commands and workload.local_ticks
publish the replay budget that was actually enforced and the executed command count; never report a covered count without its total
fill external_coverage_measurement.v1 (schema in this package: external_contract.schema) and publish it with the raw artifacts and the reproduction command

run: PYTHONPATH=src:. python3 scripts/check_external_coverage_contract.py --scope <scope> --external <document.json> --output <dir> and publish the resulting comparable/not_comparable verdict with its per-field reasons

what_a_comparable_verdict_would_and_woul.would: both numbers describe the same DUT points, the same recorded workload and the same replay bounds in the same offline mode
what_a_comparable_verdict_would_and_woul.would_not: equal search budgets, seeds, process independence, online or fixed-time coverage, or tool superiority

fresh_comparisons.note: each comparison is original vs fresh instrumented replay of the same nonce-normalised command sequence on the same pinned build

limitations: The fresh-prefix numbers are offline Verilator line/block coverage of a replay of the same recorded commands on the same pinned build; they are not a second independent fuzz campaign.
A hit_delta of zero between the original and fresh replay of the same commands is the expected identity check; it is not evidence of tool superiority or of search quality.
The saved point-map hash embeds each measurement build directory; the normalised point identity set plus the canonical denominator is the compared identity, and both are published.
Per-component denominators differ and are not additive; this package publishes no aggregate coverage.
No external tool measurement exists: the external comparison is unavailable and synthetic self-test documents are not measurements.
Input SHA256s make the package reproducible, not the original or fresh processes authenticated.
